Borealis launch:
- Target launch date: Nov 15.
- Repository: `borealis-launch`.
- Deployment region: `us-west-2`.
- In-scope modules: `notifier`, `auth-bridge`, `billing-sync`, `scheduler-v2`, `search-index`, `rate-limiter`.

Module configuration and ownership:
- `rate-limiter`: budget $25k; owner Aiko.
- `scheduler-v2`: budget $60k; priority P2.
- `search-index`: uses Redis; budget $50k; owner Tomasz.
- `auth-bridge`: uses MongoDB.
- No budget, owner, datastore, or priority recorded for `notifier` or `billing-sync`.

Engineering and operations policies/facts:
- Dependencies are declared in service manifests, validated at deploy time, and pinned/upgraded through automated pull requests.
- Deploys use the standard pipeline and require a green build; container images are scanned for vulnerabilities before promotion.
- Metrics export to the shared observability stack every 15 seconds.
- Dashboards show p50, p95, and p99 latency alongside error budgets; error budgets are reviewed weekly.
- Capacity planning is revisited at the start of every quarter.
- Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.
- Runbooks are reviewed quarterly by the owning team; the on-call handbook documents escalation paths and expected response times.
- Alerts route through the paging system per escalation policy.
- Circuit breakers open after five consecutive downstream failures.
- Retries use exponential backoff with jitter.
- Rate limiting uses a gateway token bucket per client.
- Services degrade gracefully with cached responses when dependencies are unavailable.
- Canary releases receive 5% of traffic for 30 minutes before promotion.
- Feature flags use the configuration service and roll out gradually.
- Configuration changes are peer reviewed and applied through the deployment tool.
- Mutual TLS encrypts service-to-service traffic.
- Requests propagate correlation IDs to downstream calls.
- Structured logs include request path, status code, and duration; central logs are retained for 30 days.
- Health checks hit readiness endpoints every 10 seconds.
- Synthetic probes exercise critical user journeys every minute.
- Load tests run nightly against staging; staging mirrors production topology at one-tenth scale.
- Graceful shutdown waits for in-flight requests to complete.
- Long-running jobs checkpoint progress for restart/resume.
- Idempotency keys are required on all mutating endpoints.
- Schema changes use expand-and-contract migrations.
- Connection pools are sized using the downstream capacity model.
- Garbage-collection pauses are tracked as a leading indicator of memory pressure.
- Backups are taken daily and verified weekly by restoring to a scratch cluster.
- Secrets rotate automatically every 90 days.
- Production access is granted just in time and audited.
- Data retention follows the company-wide personal-information policy.
- Cost reports are reviewed monthly with the finance partner.
- Engineers rotate through the support channel one week at a time.

- Deploys use the standard pipeline and require a green build.
- Configuration changes are peer reviewed and applied through the deployment tool.
- Staging mirrors production topology at one tenth scale.
- Load tests run nightly against staging.
- Canary releases receive five percent of traffic for thirty minutes before promotion.
- Readiness health checks run every ten seconds.
- Synthetic probes exercise critical user journeys every minute.
- Alerts route through the paging system according to the escalation policy.
- Logs are retained for thirty days in the central log store; structured logs include request path, status code, and duration.
- Requests carry a correlation ID propagated to downstream calls.
- Secrets rotate automatically every ninety days.
- Access to production is granted just in time and audited.
- Idempotency keys are required on all mutating endpoints.
- Rate limiting is enforced at the gateway with a token bucket per client.
- Circuit breakers open after five consecutive downstream failures.
- Retries use exponential backoff with jitter.
- Services degrade gracefully by serving cached responses when dependencies are down.
- Long-running jobs checkpoint progress and can resume after restart.
- Graceful shutdown waits for in-flight requests to complete.
- Connection pools are sized according to the downstream capacity model.
- Garbage-collection pauses are tracked as a leading indicator of memory pressure.
- Container images are scanned for vulnerabilities before promotion.
- Traffic is encrypted in transit with mutual TLS between services.
- Backups are taken daily and verified weekly by restoring to a scratch cluster.
- Metrics are exported to the shared observability stack every fifteen seconds.
- Dashboards show p50, p95, and p99 latency alongside error budgets.
- Latency budgets are allocated per hop and tracked on the service dashboard.
- Error budgets are reviewed in the weekly reliability meeting.
- Cost reports are reviewed monthly with the finance partner.
- Feature flags are managed through the configuration service and rolled out gradually.
- Schema changes use an expand-and-contract migration process.
- Data retention follows the company-wide policy for personal information.
- Capacity planning is revisited at the start of every quarter.
- The runbook is reviewed quarterly by the owning team.
- Engineers rotate through the support channel one week at a time.
- The on-call handbook documents escalation paths, expected response times, and the escalation policy.
- Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.

Engineering and operational policies/facts:
- Dependencies are declared in service manifests, validated at deploy time, and pinned/upgraded through automated pull requests.
- Deploys use the standard pipeline and require a green build.
- Configuration changes are peer reviewed and applied through the deployment tool.
- Staging mirrors production topology at one tenth scale.
- Load tests run nightly against staging.
- Canary releases receive five percent of traffic for thirty minutes before promotion.
- Readiness health checks run every ten seconds.
- Synthetic probes exercise critical user journeys every minute.
- Alerts route through the paging system according to the escalation policy.
- Logs are retained for thirty days in the central log store; structured logs include request path, status code, and duration.
- Requests carry a correlation ID propagated to downstream calls.
- Secrets rotate automatically every ninety days.
- Production access is granted just in time and audited.
- Idempotency keys are required on all mutating endpoints.
- Rate limiting is enforced at the gateway with a token bucket per client.
- Circuit breakers open after five consecutive downstream failures.
- Retries use exponential backoff with jitter.
- Services degrade gracefully by serving cached responses when dependencies are down.
- Long-running jobs checkpoint progress and can resume after restart.
- Graceful shutdown waits for in-flight requests to complete.
- Connection pools are sized according to the downstream capacity model.
- Garbage-collection pauses are tracked as a leading indicator of memory pressure.
- Container images are scanned for vulnerabilities before promotion.
- Traffic is encrypted in transit with mutual TLS between services.
- Backups are taken daily and verified weekly by restoring to a scratch cluster.
- Metrics are exported to the shared observability stack every fifteen seconds.
- Dashboards show p50, p95, and p99 latency alongside error budgets.
- Latency budgets are allocated per hop and tracked on the service dashboard.
- Error budgets are reviewed in the weekly reliability meeting.
- Cost reports are reviewed monthly with the finance partner.
- Feature flags are managed through the configuration service and rolled out gradually.
- Schema changes use an expand-and-contract migration process.
- Data retention follows the company-wide policy for personal information.
- Capacity planning is revisited at the start of every quarter.
- The runbook is reviewed quarterly by the owning team.
- Engineers rotate through the support channel one week at a time.
- The on-call handbook documents escalation paths, expected response times, and the escalation policy.
- Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.
